title: Exclusive namespace entry rename through daemon APIs
scope: Namespace::rename_exclusive, resident fs-rename-excl SOURCE TARGET RPC, and offline fs-rename-excl CONTAINER SOURCE TARGET
Atomic no-replace target check and entry move in one namespace update; existing entries, including same path, same-inode aliases, and dangling symlinks, return EEXIST
The ordinary rename API retains its replacing behavior; source and parent protection/path validation precede target EEXIST, while target inode flags do not change the refusal

C++ tests cover modern LevelDB and legacy storage, regular file and directory moves, hardlinks, symlink targets, metadata/xattrs, error atomicity, protections, revision/fork isolation, reopen and verification; modern coverage adds open/duplicated handle cursor continuity and GC

RPC/CLI tests cover move success, EEXIST, missing inputs, malformed RPC arity, and resident mount lease; baseline tests both occupied and absent destinations and verify namespace state, metadata, and data stay unchanged

baseline_probe.status: passed; unsupported RPC and offline CLI requests rejected without namespace state change
baseline_probe.qualification: The baseline C++ Namespace API did not include rename_exclusive, so no baseline C++ test was attempted.

explicit_exclusions: No FSKit callback, native RENAME_EXCL/renamex_np implementation, or mounted exclusive-rename behavior is included or claimed.
Synthetic link-capacity boundaries, source-parent append-only refusal, successful movement of a dangling symlink source, and the new RPC world selector are not covered by these focused tests.
The baseline differential covers resident RPC and offline CLI only because the baseline C++ API did not exist.
